findings.text: the lint row's magnitudes ("the one remaining finding and the two unformatted files") reproduce in no scope I measured: the seven touched files give 3 findings (1 F841 in tests/test_crew_promotion.py, 2 ISC004 in tests/test_gate_evidence.py) and 3 files unformatted at both 77c20349 and e5dbe176, tests/ gives 177 findings and 56 unformatted files at both revisions, and the whole repository at e5dbe176 gives 441 findings and 84 unformatted files; the row's delta claim holds in every scope, but its magnitudes name no scope a later reader can check.

the seven head logs and the base-revision control log named at line 11 are node-local temporary paths on the compute node that ran the node, so the reproduction the done_when requires is readable only while that allocation lives; I could read them only because this review runs on the same node, where they corroborate the manifest (1 failed/25 passed, 21 passed, 3 passed, and 31 FAILED in the control), and the ids and classes survive inline in the manifest and the research record, but a later reader cannot check the raw receipts.

item_verdicts.diff: read all three commits against 77c20349; the change is test fixtures plus the plan and archive records, with no test function removed, no skip or xfail added, and the removed assertion lines re-expressed as stronger properties.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names each owned file run in its own pytest process with its own --basetemp, the per-file before/after result recorded, and the red-test list recorded; the run's manifest records both, and I re-derived the base control myself rather than reading the manifest's account of it.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is that the seven files the research record's section 4 lists for this node pass at head; 30 of the 31 base ids are green at e5dbe176 (tests/test_promotion_reads_the_terminal_record.py re-run by me at 6 passed, tests/test_role_write_scope.py at 21 passed) and the one id still red is named in the run's follow_ons, which the done_when permits.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it states per-file head results, a class and cause for each of the 31 ids, and the one remaining failure as a product defect with file, lines, behaviour and a reproduction, all of which I re-ran or re-read.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the declared scope is the ten paths in the run's orientation_write_paths; every path in git diff --name-only 77c20349..e5dbe176 is inside it, nine paths in all, and the worktree is clean at e5dbe176.

justifications.durability: tests/test_crew_promotion.py:1262 asserts the worktree audit's git-call count does not move with the peer population, so the guard is measured as an invariant rather than a literal; the two load-sensitive ids left in the suite are named for a robustness follow-up.
justifications.evidence: the base control log's declared first line and its 31 FAILED ids reproduce the research record's section 4 exactly and the two sides sum to 132 tests either side, but the run's lint row (docs/evidence/archive/the-suite-is-green-at-head-landed.html:96) carries magnitudes I could not reproduce in any scope, and its raw receipts are node-local temporary paths.
justifications.fit: the new helpers follow the file-local fixture idiom of tests/test_gate_evidence.py:248 and the touched files carry the same ruff findings and unformatted-file count at base and at head.
justifications.goal_fidelity: 30 of the 31 base ids are green at e5dbe176, and the one id still red is named as a product defect in the run's follow_ons with file, lines, behaviour and a reproduction that I confirmed.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff --name-only 77c20349..e5dbe176 lies inside the ten declared write paths, and nothing outside them was written.
